name: s2n-tls-ab8b000f-blind30
instr:
# s2n-tls: repairing thirty undocumented regressions without a test suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

An application built on this library sets up encrypted links, decides whether to trust
whoever is on the far end, and moves data across them once it has, and it now gets a long
list of these wrong. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the calling code
changed. Exchanges that used to complete now fail or complete on terms neither side asked
for, and answers that used to come back right now come back wrong.

Agreeing the terms at the start of an exchange goes astray in several ways. An application
that takes private key signing into its own hands and then asks for the resulting signature
to be checked before it is used never gets past the opening exchange: the attempt is
abandoned and the link torn down. A server that settles on an older version of the protocol
writes the marker that signals a forced downgrade into the random value it sends even in
cases where it should not, and the peer, reading that marker, tears the link down. When
what the peer offers for key agreement does not include the server's first choice, the
group picked for the exchange, or the group the peer is told to try again with, is not one
that both sides actually support, so exchanges that mix classical groups with post-quantum
ones settle on an unexpected group or fail. Agreeing on which application protocol to run,
